'''Pia Dandiya''' (born 1986/1987)<ref>https://www.naplesnews.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/10/17/qa-with-pia-dandiya-democratic-nominee-for-congressional-district-22/91611633007/</ref> is an American educator, former technology executive, and politician who is the [[United States House of Representatives|United States representative-elect]] from [[Florida's 22nd congressional district]]. A former high school principal and [[White House Fellows|White House Fellow]], she later led public-sector initiatives at [[Apple Inc.]]<ref name="fp-launch">{{cite news |title='Floridians deserve better': Pia Dandiya launches campaign to flip Brian Mast's seat in CD 21 |url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/740914-floridians-deserve-better-pia-dandiya-launches-campaign-to-flip-brian-masts-seat-in-cd-21/ |work=[[Florida Politics]] |date=June 2, 2025 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref> She was the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee for [[Florida's 22nd congressional district]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Florida|2026 election]], defeating Republican nominee [[Casey Askar]].<ref name="pbp-primary">{{cite news |title=Pia Dandiya wins Democratic primary for US House 22 |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/news/politics/elections/congressional/2026/08/18/us-house-22-democratic-primary-pits-pia-dandiya-and-kaysia-earley/91247294007/ |work=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |date=August 18, 2026 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Dandiya was born and raised in [[Palm Beach County, Florida]].<ref name="guardian">{{cite news |last=Luscombe |first=Richard |title=Florida Democrat switches districts after DeSantis redistricting |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/06/priya-dandiya-florida-redistricting-democrat |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=August 6, 2026 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref> She is a second-generation American; her parents immigrated to the United States from India.<ref name="guardian" /> Her parents moved from [[Jaipur]] to [[Jupiter, Florida]], in the 1980s, where she was raised; her father practiced medicine and her mother founded a [[Montessori education|Montessori]] school.<ref name="nia">{{cite news |title=Leading with heart: How Pia Dandiya is reimagining public service |url=https://www.newindiaabroad.com/english/features/leading-with-heart-how-pia-dandiya-is-reimagining-public-service |work=New India Abroad |date=August 25, 2025 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref>

Dandiya earned a Bachelor of Arts in government from [[Harvard University]] and a Master of Education from [[Boston University]].<ref name="lokvani">{{cite news |title=Pia Dandiya appointed White House Fellow |url=https://www.lokvani.com/lokvani/article.php?article_id=17165 |work=Lokvani |date=December 11, 2020 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==
Dandiya began her career in Boston as a [[Teach for America]] corps member, teaching middle school mathematics, and later managed teacher leadership development for Teach for America in New York.<ref name="lokvani" /> At age 28, she became the founding principal of Democracy Prep Endurance High School in [[Harlem]], New York.<ref name="lokvani" /><ref name="bs">{{cite news |title=Indian ambassador in US Taranjit Sandhu interacts with White House Fellows |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/indian-ambassador-in-us-taranjit-sandhu-interacts-with-white-house-fellows-121070200093_1.html |work=[[Business Standard]] |date=July 2, 2021 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref>

Dandiya was named to the 2020–2021 class of [[White House Fellows]] and placed at the [[United States Department of Education]].<ref name="lokvani" /><ref name="guardian" /> Her fellowship spanned the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump]] and [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden]] administrations and included work with the [[Domestic Policy Council]] on child development, school nutrition, and access to education.<ref name="fp-launch" />

Beginning in January 2022, Dandiya worked at [[Apple Inc.|Apple]], where she led public-sector partnerships and initiatives focused on education, health care, and government services.<ref name="fp-launch" />

== U.S. House of Representatives ==
=== Elections ===
==== 2026 ====
[[File:Florida's 21st congressional district (since 2023) (new version).svg|thumb|[[Florida's 21st congressional district]]]]Dandiya announced her candidacy for [[Florida's 21st congressional district]] in June 2025, challenging Republican incumbent [[Brian Mast]].<ref name="fp-launch" /> State records showed she had been registered as a Republican until switching her registration to Democratic in 2020.<ref name="fp-launch" />

After Governor [[Ron DeSantis]] pushed through a mid-decade congressional redistricting in 2026, Dandiya moved her campaign to the newly drawn 22nd district, an open seat.<ref name="guardian" /> The redrawn district extends from western Palm Beach County through Broward County toward the [[Gulf Coast of the United States|Gulf Coast]].<ref name="pbp-primary" /> Incumbent Democrat [[Lois Frankel]] chose to run in the neighboring [[Florida's 23rd congressional district|23rd district]].<ref name="hill">{{cite news |title=Dandiya, Askar duke it out for Frankel's redistricted Florida House seat |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6028302-dandiya-askar-florida-house-primary/ |work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |date=August 18, 2026 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref>

On August 18, 2026, Dandiya defeated attorney Kaysia Earley in the Democratic primary, winning 68.6 percent of the vote according to certified results.<ref name="nyt">{{cite web |title=Florida 22nd Congressional District Primary Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/08/18/us/elections/results-florida-us-house-22-primary.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=August 18, 2026 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref> She faced Republican nominee [[Casey Askar]] in the November 3 general election.<ref name="hill" />

Dandiya's platform focused on lowering the cost of living, including housing, child care, health care, and insurance; strengthening public education, including universal [[Pre-kindergarten|pre-K]]; and protecting [[Social Security (United States)|Social Security]], [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]], [[Medicaid]], and reproductive rights.<ref name="pbp-primary" /> She has called for ending tariffs, saying their costs have reached ordinary consumers.<ref name="cbs">{{cite news |title=Florida District 22 congressional race |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/florida-district-22-congressional-race-republican-primary/ |work=[[CBS News]] Miami |date=August 7, 2026 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref> Her government-reform proposals include banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks and limiting the influence of lobbyists.<ref name="ballotpedia">{{cite news |title=Competitive race expected in Florida's 22nd Congressional District, which Biden won in 2020 and Trump won in 2024 |url=https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/09/05/competitive-race-expected-in-floridas-22nd-congressional-district-which-biden-won-in-2020-and-trump-won-in-2024/ |work=[[Ballotpedia]] News |date=September 5, 2026 |access-date=September 28, 2026}}</ref>

Her campaign has been endorsed by [[EMILY's List]], the Florida [[AFL–CIO]], Florida Democratic Party chair [[Nikki Fried]], and Frankel, and in August 2026 the [[Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee]] added her to its "Red to Blue" program.<ref name="guardian" /> The ''[[South Florida Sun Sentinel]]'' editorial board endorsed her in the Democratic primary.<ref name="cbs" /> By early August 2026, her fundraising had exceeded $2 million.<ref name="guardian" />

== Political positions ==
On healthcare, Dandiya supports, as ways to lower costs, allowing Medicare to negotiate [[prescription drug prices]] and restoring the [[Affordable Care Act]] subsidies that had been previously cancelled. With Social Security, Dandiya has the perspective of raising the cap on income subject to Social Security tax as one way to fund Social Security for the future. She said in a 2026 interview on [[WFLX]] that:<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hussey |first=Kate |date=2026-10-29 |title=Florida District 22 candidates Casey Askar, Pia Dandiya clash over affordability |url=https://www.wflx.com/2026/10/29/florida-district-22-candidates-casey-askar-pia-dandiya-clash-over-affordability/ |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=[[WFLX]] |language=en}}</ref><blockquote>People have been spending years saving into that Social Security, expecting to have a retirement in dignity. In my view, there is no world in which we can walk back on that promise.</blockquote>

== Personal life ==
Dandiya lives in [[Palm Beach Gardens, Florida]], with her husband and son.<ref name="fp-launch" />
